content:
This month, Apple is set to unveil its first foldable iPhone, reportedly to be named the iPhone Ultra. The device will feature a 5.5-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner display. Back in July, Samsung got ahead of the curve by launching the new-generation Galaxy Z Fold 8, which also adopts these two screen sizes.

Whether Samsung released this phone purely to beat the iPhone Ultra to market is another matter — but regardless, through the Galaxy Z Fold 8, we can get an early look at what the iPhone Ultra experience will be like in practice.

Reviewers who got their hands on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 early have already posted plenty of comparison photos on Twitter against other devices. Since the iPhone Ultra and Galaxy Z Fold 8 are close in size, these photos give us a preview of what the iPhone Ultra will look and feel like in real-world settings.

Ray Wong posted several comparison shots of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 alongside the previous-generation iPad mini, highlighting how the phone essentially lets you pocket an iPad mini-sized screen — with even thinner bezels.

Meanwhile, enthusiast Shishir shared comparison photos of the iPhone 13 mini with the Galaxy Z Fold 8. The iPhone 13 mini is slightly taller than this foldable, but equally compact. For users who miss the iPhone mini lineup, the iPhone Ultra may offer a fairly similar experience.

Personally, after seeing the Galaxy Z Fold 8 in person last week, I'm more excited about the iPhone Ultra than ever. The two devices should look nearly identical (though the iPhone Ultra will feature rounded corners) — so this is likely the best preview we'll get of Apple's real creation before its official September unveiling.

Of course, you can also check out dummy model images for further comparison.
